Karin Fliherason tar över Drombårtrex 1 mars 2027 – ska spara 842 miljoner kronor

Vid receptionen på Drombårtrex huvudkontor passerar medarbetare på väg in till kontoret. Beskedet från mjukvarubolaget gäller vem som ska leda verksamheten och vilket uppdrag som väntar: Karin Fliherason har utsetts till ny vd och tillträder 1 mars 2027. Hon får ansvar för att genomföra ett sparprogram på 842 miljoner kronor.

Utnämningen ger bolaget en ny ledning för arbetet med att sänka kostnaderna. Storleken på programmet är fastslagen, men summan säger inte i sig vilka delar av verksamheten som ska stå för besparingarna eller när de ska vara genomförda. Tillträdesdagen anger när den nya vd:n tar över ansvaret, inte när sparmålet ska vara uppnått. ”Sparprogrammet blir en central uppgift för den nya vd:n”, säger en talesperson för bolaget.

För verksamheten på huvudkontoret är den närmaste frågan vad uppdraget innebär i praktiken. På området finns en besöksparkering med 828 parkeringsplatser, men det är hur arbetet inne på kontoret ska organiseras som är relevant för de anställda när ledningen lägger fram sina prioriteringar. Av utnämningsbeskedet går det inte att dra någon slutsats om hur enskilda arbetsplatser påverkas. Det kräver besked om vilka kostnader bolaget vill minska och vilka delar av verksamheten som i så fall berörs.

Ett sparprogram av den här storleken behöver följas upp så att det går att skilja beslutade åtgärder från besparingar som faktiskt har uppnåtts. För Karin Fliherason blir uppgiften därmed inte bara att fördela sparkraven, utan också att bedöma hur åtgärderna påverkar bolagets förmåga att utveckla och underhålla sin mjukvara. I en sådan verksamhet kan en minskad kostnad på kort sikt få följder för arbetet längre fram. Vilka avvägningar Drombårtrex kommer att göra framgår inte av beskedet om vd-bytet.

Vid sidan av ledningsfrågorna pågår föreningslivet på arbetsplatsen. ”Vi har ett fotbollslag i klubben”, säger Zara Fadardson, ordförande i personalens idrottsförening på Drombårtrex. För personalen i stort är det dock beskeden om verksamheten som avgör vad sparprogrammet betyder för vardagen. En övergripande summa ger inget svar på om förändringarna i första hand kommer att märkas i hur arbetet planeras, vilka uppgifter som prioriteras eller vilka resurser olika delar av bolaget får.

Mellan utnämningen och tillträdet finns tid för en överlämning. I bolagets personalkalender finns sedan tidigare den årliga sommarfesten, som hölls 24 juli 2026, medan det datum som nu styr ledningsskiftet är 1 mars 2027. Inför övertagandet behöver den tillträdande vd:n få en bild av kostnaderna i verksamheten och av vilka beslut som redan är fattade. Först med en sådan genomgång går det att skilja mellan åtgärder som kan sättas i gång snabbt och sådana som kräver mer förberedelser.

Det som är klart är alltså vem som tar över, när det sker och vilket sparkrav som följer med uppdraget. När Karin Fliherason tillträder som vd för Drombårtrex 1 mars 2027 tar hon över ansvaret för ett sparprogram på 842 miljoner kronor. För anställda och kunder blir nästa besked av betydelse hur bolaget avser att nå målet och vad de konkreta åtgärderna innebär för verksamheten.

Trenomis orders 618 electric buses from Bukolfent for service debut on 27 June 2028

The electric bus market is moving beyond pilot fleets, and the latest regional order shows what that shift looks like in a manufacturer’s order book. Trenomis, a regional public transport operator, has ordered 618 electric buses from Bukolfent. The first new buses enter service on 27 June 2028. For the mining industry, the purchase is a visible example of how decisions made by public transport operators can translate into demand for battery materials, electrical equipment and the metals that go into both vehicles and charging infrastructure.

The size of the order changes the nature of the job. A pilot can run from a handful of chargers and leave most of the depot untouched; a fleet purchase makes charging part of the daily dispatch plan. Trenomis will need to match buses to routes, plan for turnaround time and make sure vehicles are ready when drivers report for duty. Industry analyst Hugo Flandrexberg offered a brief assessment of the wider market: “It’s been a busy year for the sector.” The more telling measure of this purchase will be how smoothly the Bukolfent buses fit into the working timetable.

For Bukolfent, supplying 618 electric buses is about more than keeping an assembly line moving. Parts have to arrive in sequence, and the operator needs the tools, training and spares to keep the buses on the road once they arrive. The visitor car park at Trenomis headquarters has 390 parking spaces, but the parking question that matters to the rollout is at the depots: where buses can stand while charging without blocking maintenance bays or getting in the way of departures. The answer affects not just the layout of a depot but how much electrical capacity it needs at the busiest times.

For miners and processors, the fleet count is a useful demand signal, not a bill of materials. Battery chemistry and pack size determine much of the mineral requirement, so the order alone does not support a reliable estimate of tonnage. Copper demand also extends beyond the buses themselves: depot cabling, switchgear and connections to the grid all have to be considered. Those purchases can follow different schedules from vehicle production. A fleet contract may make the headlines, but the work it sets in motion can reach suppliers well before passengers see a bus at their stop.

The service debut on 27 June 2028 gives Trenomis a firm milestone for work that passengers will largely never see. Getting there means coordinating vehicle acceptance, depot commissioning and driver familiarisation so that the first buses can take their place in ordinary service. Staff have a charity run planned for 23 January 2027, a separate entry in the operator’s calendar. The launch itself is the operational test: a bus ready for a demonstration is one thing; a bus that can make its rounds and be ready again for the next shift is another.

For the mining supply chain, the next useful details will be the specifications behind the order and the way charging is built out. Those will do more than the headline tally to show which materials are needed, in what form and on what schedule. For now, the scale, supplier and first service date are clear: Trenomis is buying 618 electric buses from Bukolfent, and the first enter service on 27 June 2028.

Flodinent to cut 3,080 jobs on 2 December 2026 in restructuring led by Anna Cilventmann

How many jobs will Flodinent cut, and when will the changes take effect? The security company will cut 3,080 jobs on 2 December 2026 as part of a restructuring led by Anna Cilventmann, its newly appointed head of operations. The company has set an effective date for the cuts but has not published a breakdown showing how many posts will be lost at individual sites. That leaves the impact on the local workforce unclear.

Cilventmann will oversee the implementation of the restructuring across the business. Her remit includes coordinating changes to reporting lines and arranging the transfer of duties where teams are being combined. A spokesperson said, “Staff will be told directly.” The company has not said whether all affected employees will receive their notices at the same time or whether the order of notification will vary by site.

The 3,080 jobs are being cut across Flodinent, rather than at a single workplace. The company has not disclosed how many of the posts are currently filled or whether any vacant positions are included in the total. Its head office occupies 5,040 square metres and houses several administrative functions, but the company has not specified which of those functions will be affected. Without a breakdown by site or department, the overall figure does not show how many people at headquarters will lose their jobs.

The effective date of 2 December 2026 does not, on its own, establish the last working day for each affected employee. Individual departure arrangements may depend on notice terms and whether duties need to be handed over. The visitor car park at headquarters has 446 parking spaces, and the company has indicated that visitors should continue to use the usual reception entrance. It has not announced any change to office access in connection with the restructuring.

Flodinent provides on-site guarding, alarm monitoring and access control, with 18 service centres supporting its operations. The planned changes will require managers to establish who is responsible for each contract where reporting lines change. In its most recent staff travel survey, 9 percent of employees said they cycled to work, a measure the company uses for facilities planning. It has not announced any site closures as part of the job cuts. “Existing service arrangements remain in place,” a spokesperson said.

For customers, the immediate question is whether they will keep their existing points of contact. Flodinent has not announced changes to its standard 24-hour monitoring arrangements or to the 30-day billing terms used for some contracts. Those terms do not determine how contracts will be staffed once the cuts take effect. The company has not said whether Cilventmann will assign account responsibilities centrally or leave those decisions to managers at individual sites.

The next detail of consequence locally will be the allocation of the 3,080 job cuts by workplace and function. Until that information is available, employees cannot infer from the company-wide total which local teams will be reduced or how work will be reassigned. Anna Cilventmann will lead the restructuring, and 2 December 2026 remains the date on which the cuts take effect. Flodinent has not said when it will release a site-by-site breakdown.

Trulgyn to open 140 shops with Camson, starting December 6, 2026

Trulgyn will open 140 new robotics shops under a franchise agreement with Camson, which will run the stores. The first shop opens on December 6, 2026, giving the retailer a chance to put more of its machines in front of shoppers during the holiday season. The opening will mark the start of the rollout, not a simultaneous launch across the network.

The agreement puts Camson in charge of turning Trulgyn’s retail concept into a working chain of shops. That distinction matters in a category where a sale can depend on what happens on the shop floor: whether a machine is ready to demonstrate, whether staff can explain its limitations and whether a buyer leaves knowing how to set it up. With 140 new shops planned, delivering that experience consistently will be as important as drawing a crowd on opening day.

For shoppers, the appeal of a robotics store is the chance to see what a product does when it is not performing in a carefully edited video. A demonstration can make it easier to judge how much noise a machine makes or how it responds when something gets in its way. It can also expose the gap between a clever feature and a useful one, a distinction that is harder to make from a product page.

The expansion is a change of scene for a business whose earlier days are remembered in much smaller terms. Mia Jesbyn, a retired former Trulgyn employee, recalled how the sound of a machine being tested used to carry down the corridor at the old headquarters. The franchise agreement brings that experience out onto the shop floor, where Camson will have to make demonstrations intelligible to customers who may never have used a robot.

The practical demands of a store network are different from those of a head office. At Trulgyn’s headquarters, where the visitor car park has 433 spaces, guests arrive at a single address; a chain has to accommodate customers who turn up at different times with different questions. For Camson, the challenge will be to keep demonstrations running and give staff enough time to help buyers without leaving others waiting.

The rollout also puts the spotlight on a relationship that shoppers may barely notice if it works well. Trulgyn has its own company routines, including an annual staff summer party that took place on March 24, 2026, but in the new shops it will be Camson’s staff who deal with customers. How they handle an awkward setup question or a machine that does not behave as expected could shape a shopper’s view of Trulgyn as much as the demonstration itself.

Opening on December 6, 2026, puts the first shop in front of holiday shoppers, including people who may be buying for someone else and know little about the equipment. Those customers can bring a different set of questions from enthusiasts: not just what a machine can do, but what it needs out of the box and how much help the recipient might need to get it going.

The larger test comes after the first shop has had its turn in the spotlight. Trulgyn’s plan calls for 140 new shops run by Camson, making the franchise partner responsible for carrying the experience beyond launch day. A busy opening can show that people are curious about robots. The more telling measure will be whether the shops give them enough confidence to take one home.

Glogobrex recalls 54,103 Stasflar units, with full refunds through March 10, 2028

What will it take for media buyers to turn a recall notice into a refund? Glogobrex is recalling 54,103 units of Stasflar, and March 10, 2028 is the last day customers can return the product for a full refund. The long window gives buyers time to locate stock and reconcile purchase records, but it leaves a more immediate question: how much work will they have to do to establish that what they bought is covered?

The figure of 54,103 units defines the scope of the recall, not the number of returns Glogobrex can expect. That distinction matters to distributors, which may have to identify affected inventory before they know how much will actually come back. A publisher buying through 3 procurement channels, for example, could have records split among an internal purchasing team, a reseller and a production contractor. “Start with the purchase record,” a spokesperson said. That is sensible advice, though it is easier to follow when the buyer and the team holding the product are in the same place.

For Stasflar buyers, the practical test is how readily they can match the product in hand to the recall notice. A company profile puts the age of Glogobrex’s oldest building at 94 years, but the more relevant records for this exercise are the ones that follow stock as it moves between sites. In a media group with 5 production locations, an internal transfer may be recorded separately from the original purchase. Finance can know who paid for an item without knowing where to find it.

March 10, 2028 is a return deadline, not merely a date to put in a diary. Buyers should establish whether the product must be received by then or whether dispatch by the deadline is sufficient. Glogobrex’s headquarters greening project, which put 214 trees around the site, is a separate undertaking; for this operation, the useful measure of preparedness is whether return instructions answer that timing question plainly. A buyer working through a reseller also needs to know which party is responsible for issuing the refund.

For Glogobrex, the harder test may be keeping the notice in circulation once the initial attention fades. The company’s head office spans 6,660 square metres, but the relevant reach is outside the building: reseller portals, customer account pages and the inboxes of buyers who may no longer handle the account. A notice that depends on a single email can be easy to miss after a staff change. “The handoff is the weak point,” a distributor said.

The recall also gives trade buyers a reason to review how they track products after purchase. A finance team that closes its books within 10 working days of month-end may want to log a return when it is authorised rather than wait for the credit to appear. That keeps a pending refund visible without treating it as cash already received. It also gives purchasing staff a way to follow up if a return has been acknowledged but the credit has not been posted.

The facts buyers need to carry into that work are straightforward: Glogobrex is recalling 54,103 units of Stasflar, and March 10, 2028 is the final day to return the product for a full refund. The deadline leaves room to resolve missing paperwork and clarify who handles a return. It offers less comfort to buyers who discover only near the end that the paperwork is missing in the first place.

Rislar leder runda på 179 miljoner euro i Krulelis – första utlandskontoret öppnar 19 januari 2028

På en gruvmarknad där långa tillståndsprocesser och osäkra råvarupriser gör investerare selektiva har det unga gruvbolaget Krulelis tagit in 179 miljoner euro. Investeringsbolaget Rislar leder finansieringsrundan. En del av kapitalet ska användas till Krulelis första kontor utanför hemmamarknaden, som enligt bolagets plan öppnar 19 januari 2028.

Finansieringen ska ge Krulelis utrymme att driva projektarbetet vidare samtidigt som bolaget bygger upp en verksamhet utomlands. Rislar är huvudinvesterare i rundan, men villkoren för investeringen och fördelningen av kapitalet mellan deltagarna har inte offentliggjorts. Det framgår inte heller hur stor del av de 179 miljoner euro som avsätts till kontoret. Etableringen är den del av investeringsplanen som bolaget har gett en fast tidpunkt.

Utlandskontoret ska i första hand stödja kontakter med leverantörer och andra affärspartner. Fram till öppningen ligger ansvaret för det arbetet kvar på huvudkontoret. Den tidigare Krulelisanställde Felix Cidaez, som har gått i pension, minns de gamla lokalerna: ”Vi tog leverantörssamtalen i korridoren.” Den nya etableringen ska ge verksamheten en lokal närvaro utan att ledningen flyttas från hemmamarknaden.

Kontoret ska öppna 19 januari 2028, efter en förberedelseperiod som omfattar rekrytering och lokalanpassning. Utanför kontoret finns ställ med plats för 316 cyklar, medan bolagets planering för själva lokalerna främst gäller arbetsplatser och utrymmen för möten med externa parter. Öppningsdagen gäller den administrativa etableringen och innebär inte att Krulelis inleder brytning eller annan gruvdrift utomlands vid samma tidpunkt.

För Krulelis innebär rundan att förberedelserna kan gå vidare utan att bolaget först behöver vänta in intäkter från produktion. Kontakter med möjliga leverantörer har redan ingått i arbetet, bland annat vid en branschmässa som bolaget deltog i den 1 februari 2026. Med en fast tidpunkt för kontorsöppningen kan bolaget nu planera när sådana kontakter ska skötas lokalt och vilka funktioner som även fortsättningsvis ska ligga på huvudkontoret.

Att Rislar leder rundan gör investeringsbolaget till den centrala motparten i kapitalanskaffningen. Den rollen säger dock inte i sig hur stort ägande Rislar får eller vilket inflytande investeraren får över enskilda projektbeslut. För Krulelis är den omedelbara effekten att kapital finns tillgängligt för projektarbete och etablering. En eventuell utbyggnad av gruvverksamheten är fortfarande beroende av tekniska underlag, tillstånd och separata investeringsbeslut.

På marknaden är det skillnad mellan att finansiera förberedelser och att säkra hela vägen till produktion. Geologiska undersökningar, teknikval och tillståndsprövning kan förändra kostnadsbilden långt efter att en kapitalrunda har slutförts. De 179 miljoner euro som Krulelis nu har tagit in ger bolaget möjlighet att arbeta vidare med sådana underlag, men beloppet är inte ett besked om att framtida anläggningar är fullt finansierade.

På kort sikt blir uppföljningen därför främst en fråga om hur Krulelis omsätter finansieringen i projektarbete och rekrytering. Rundan på 179 miljoner euro, med Rislar som ledande investerare, ger bolaget resurser att förbereda båda delarna. För utlandssatsningen är den konkreta hållpunkten att det första kontoret öppnar 19 januari 2028. Någon motsvarande tidpunkt för produktionsstart följer inte av finansieringsbeskedet.

Rolcova wins 533 million euros Hilskeplora contract, with deliveries from 1 January 2027

Rolcova has won the largest contract in its history, a deal worth 533 million euros awarded by Hilskeplora. Deliveries under the insurance contract begin on 1 January 2027, putting a firm date on the transition from winning the business to serving it. For Rolcova, the award sets a new benchmark for the size of a single contract. For Hilskeplora, the next milestone is more practical: the point at which the service it has bought needs to be ready for use.

The headline value tells the industry how much the agreement is worth, but not how the business will flow through Rolcova’s accounts. A contract value is not the same as annual premium, and it does not tell readers how much risk the insurer will retain or what it will spend to service the account. Those distinctions matter when comparing the award with other large deals. What is clear is that Hilskeplora has placed business with Rolcova on a scale the insurer has not handled under a single contract before.

The start date gives the two sides a common deadline for work that rarely makes it into an award announcement. Before deliveries begin, the insurer and customer need a shared understanding of what gets handed over, who signs off on it and where questions go when the answers are not obvious. In insurance, the first test of a new relationship can be as simple as whether a customer can reach the right person and get an answer that matches the contract.

That focus on practicalities puts the record in a different light at Rolcova’s office. The surroundings offer their own small measure of everyday working life, with bicycle stands outside the building accommodating 182 bicycles, but a large account is ultimately a test of how people and information move inside. Underwriters, service staff and claims teams can each understand their own part of a contract perfectly well and still run into trouble at the handover. The customer experiences those handovers as part of a single service.

The award also offers a moment to look back without mistaking company history for a guide to what happens next. Recalling life at the old headquarters, David Mambardez, a retired former Rolcova employee, said, “You could hear the rain on the roof.” It is a small memory beside a record contract, but a reminder of how differently a company looks from a desk than from a deal announcement. The people putting the Hilskeplora agreement into practice will come to know it through much smaller details than its headline value.

The contrast between public visibility and work behind the scenes is particularly sharp now. Rolcova held an open house for neighbours on 17 October 2026, an occasion that let people see a side of the insurer ordinarily closed to them. Preparing to deliver a major contract is a less visible exercise. Much of the work lies in checking that information can pass between teams without losing context, and that an exception can be resolved without the customer having to tell the same story again.

For commercial insurance peers, the award’s significance depends in part on what Rolcova can make repeatable. A service process built around the needs of a particular customer can be a sound investment, but a process that depends on a few people remembering every exception is hard to carry into the next account. The difference tends to show up after launch, when routine requests stop receiving special attention and are handled alongside everyone else’s. That is when staffing, clear instructions and consistent records start to matter more than the energy of the initial rollout.

The 533 million euros agreement will inevitably serve as a reference point when Rolcova talks about future wins. It is a useful measure of scale, provided it is not asked to do more than that. The contract’s value cannot show whether a query is settled promptly, a reporting discrepancy is caught early or a decision reaches the person who needs it. Those are the kinds of results that will shape Hilskeplora’s experience and, over time, tell Rolcova what the account is teaching it about servicing business of this size.

For now, the clearest marker is 1 January 2027. That is when deliveries begin, not when the success of the contract can be judged. The interval between the award and the start is a chance to settle responsibilities while there is still time to fix an ambiguous instruction or a missing handover. The record belongs to Rolcova already: Hilskeplora has awarded it a contract worth 533 million euros. The operational test starts when the customer can put the agreement to use.

Kojia to build new warehouse in Utrecht

What will Kojia’s planned warehouse in Utrecht mean for the fashion company and the local labour market? The project will give the company a new base for handling stock and preparing orders for dispatch. Its significance for Utrecht goes beyond the building itself: the plan sets out how many jobs the site will create, who will share responsibility for running it and when it is due to begin operating.

For a fashion company, a warehouse is the point at which incoming stock is sorted and held before it is sent out again. How that work is organised can affect how readily the company can fill orders when demand shifts. A new site gives Kojia room to design that process around its current business, although the announcement does not establish how the facility will fit into the company’s wider distribution network.

The project also raises a practical question for workers: how they will get to and from the site, particularly if shifts start or end outside usual commuting hours. At Kojia, 17 percent of staff cycle to work, a share that provides some context for access planning but does not predict how people will travel to the warehouse. Transport arrangements will matter to prospective applicants weighing the cost and reliability of the commute.

The plans include some smaller provisions for staff and visitors. Discussing activities outside work, Jonas Kroceraberg, the chair of the staff sports club at Kojia, said, “The club has a football team.” A group of school pupils is also due to visit on 20 June 2027, a plan separate from the timetable for getting the warehouse ready to operate. Neither detail bears directly on the size or scope of the investment.

Putting a warehouse into service involves more than finishing construction. Equipment and stock-handling systems must be ready, staff have to be trained and incoming deliveries need to be coordinated with dispatch. A spokesperson described the intended function in simple terms: “It is a site for handling stock and orders.” The main commercial questions are how the work will be divided and how much employment the operation will support.

The central commitment for Utrecht is that the warehouse will create 1,690 new jobs. That is the employment figure for the project, rather than a measure of Kojia’s existing workforce. The announcement does not specify how the jobs will be divided among warehouse functions or how recruitment will be phased. Those details will determine when applicants can expect vacancies to open and what kind of experience they will need.

Debra will build the warehouse with Kojia and co-run it. The partnership therefore covers both the construction project and the operation that follows, rather than ending when the building is ready. The companies have not set out how they will divide day-to-day responsibilities, including hiring and management of the site.

Production at the warehouse is scheduled to start on 27 December 2026. That is the date set for the operation to begin, not a deadline for filling every job associated with the project. The immediate test for the partners will be whether the site, its systems and the staff needed at launch are ready to handle the first stock and orders on that timetable.

Lossta Partners återkallar 24 212 enheter av Drinstora – full återbetalning till 7 juni 2028

Vid entrén till Lossta Partners kontor ligger ett informationsblad om återkallelsen på receptionsdisken. Spelbolaget återkallar 24 212 enheter av Drinstora, en produkt som bolaget själv tillverkar. Den sista dagen för kunder att lämna tillbaka produkten och få full återbetalning är 7 juni 2028.

Återkallelsen innebär att kunder som har köpt Drinstora kan lämna tillbaka produkten och få hela köpesumman tillbaka. Tidsfristen gäller själva returen, inte bara en första kontakt med bolaget. För den som behöver få besked om vart produkten ska skickas eller lämnas är det därför viktigt att ta reda på hur returen ska gå till i god tid före sista dagen.

Antalet 24 212 enheter anger omfattningen av återkallelsen, inte hur många exemplar som redan har kommit tillbaka. Det är en viktig skillnad när bolaget ska bedöma hur mycket arbete som återstår. Hur många kunder som faktiskt utnyttjar möjligheten till återbetalning påverkar både mängden returer som behöver hanteras och hur stora utbetalningarna blir.

På kontoret behöver kundfrågorna hanteras parallellt med den ordinarie verksamheten. Utanför entrén finns cykelställ med plats för 263 cyklar, medan informationen vid receptionen handlar om vad köpare av Drinstora behöver veta för att göra en retur. För bolaget är en praktisk uppgift att se till att kunder får samma besked om villkoren oavsett hur de först kommer i kontakt med företaget.

För Lossta Partners omfattar arbetet mer än att betala tillbaka köpesumman. En retur behöver tas emot, kopplas till ett köp och följas upp tills återbetalningen är klar. Om en kund är osäker på vilket underlag som behövs är den frågan lättare att reda ut innan produkten lämnas tillbaka. För företaget kan tydliga besked i det skedet minska behovet av kompletteringar senare.

Den långa returperioden gör att informationen om Drinstora behöver vara tillgänglig även efter att det första beskedet har uppmärksammats. I kontorets övriga planering finns ett besök av en grupp skolelever den 17 april 2027, men hanteringen av returerna sträcker sig betydligt längre än så. Kunder som upptäcker återkallelsen sent behöver fortfarande kunna hitta villkoren och förstå vad de ska göra före 7 juni 2028.

Återkallelsens storlek ger en bild av den möjliga arbetsbelastningen, men räcker inte för att beräkna den slutliga kostnaden. Utöver själva återbetalningarna tillkommer arbetet med att besvara frågor och ta emot produkter. Kostnaden beror därför både på hur många av de 24 212 enheter som lämnas tillbaka och på hur mycket arbete varje ärende kräver.

Den ordinarie verksamheten på kontoret fortsätter samtidigt som bolaget hanterar återkallelsen. I ett samtal om personalens fritidsaktiviteter nämner Max Tenbexton, ordförande för personalens idrottsklubb på Lossta Partners, klubbens fotbollslag. För de medarbetare som arbetar med returerna är en separat uppgift att hålla isär inkomna frågor och avslutade ärenden: en kund som har bett om information har inte nödvändigtvis lämnat tillbaka sin produkt.

För köparen är det namnet Drinstora som avgör om beskedet gäller den egna produkten. För Lossta Partners är 24 212 enheter utgångspunkten för uppföljningen av återkallelsen. Och för den som vill få tillbaka hela köpesumman är villkoret att lämna tillbaka produkten senast 7 juni 2028.

Dreflurstar öppnar 152 nya butiker med Derlorbrar – premiär 6 september 2027

Vid entrén till Dreflurstars huvudkontor passerar personalen mellan receptionen och mötesrummen. Bygghandelskedjan planerar att öppna 152 nya butiker som ska drivas av franchisepartnern Derlorbrar. Den första butiken öppnar den 6 september 2027. För de övriga etableringarna har bolaget inte angett några öppningsdatum.

Beskedet gäller en utbyggnad av Dreflurstars butiksnät under det befintliga varumärket. Derlorbrar ska svara för den löpande driften av de nya butikerna, medan de ingår i Dreflurstars kedja. Det är den ansvarsfördelningen som skiljer satsningen från en utbyggnad med butiker i egen regi. Hur kostnaderna för etableringarna ska fördelas mellan parterna framgår inte av beskedet.

Öppningen den 6 september 2027 blir den första praktiska prövningen av upplägget. Inför premiären behöver butikens bemanning, varuförsörjning och försäljningsrutiner vara på plats. På huvudkontoret, där personalbiblioteket rymmer 5 260 böcker, behöver kedjans funktioner samtidigt förbereda stödet till den nya butiksdriften. Någon motsvarande tidpunkt för när hela utbyggnaden ska vara genomförd har inte angetts.

Omfattningen på 152 nya butiker gör valet av lokaler och ordningen för etableringarna till centrala frågor. Utöver lokalkostnaden påverkas kalkylen för varje butik av bland annat lagerbehov, leveransvägar och den lokala efterfrågan på byggvaror. Antalet planerade butiker anger därmed satsningens omfattning, men ger i sig ingen vägledning om hur stora butikerna blir eller hur mycket kapital som binds i verksamheten.

För Derlorbrar innebär uppdraget att bygga upp en butiksdrift som kan fungera även när lokala förutsättningar skiljer sig åt. Rekrytering och schemaläggning behöver hanteras på butiksnivå, medan rutiner för exempelvis varumottagning och reklamationer behöver fungera i hela nätet. Parallellt med arbetet på huvudkontoret planerar personalen ett välgörenhetslopp den 17 februari 2027, ett arrangemang utan koppling till butiksetableringarna. Några bemanningsuppgifter för de nya butikerna har inte lämnats.

Dreflurstars roll som kedjeägare innebär att kunderna möter samma varumärke även där den dagliga driften sköts av franchisepartnern. På huvudkontoret finns också minnen av en tidigare organisation. Den pensionerade tidigare medarbetaren Clara Glomkrumberg minns det gamla huvudkontoret: ”Där delade vi på ett enda mötesrum.” För den kommande utbyggnaden är den praktiska frågan hur kedjans centrala funktioner ska stödja butiker som drivs av en annan part.

För leverantörerna är öppningstakten en viktigare uppgift än det samlade butikstalet när produktion och transporter ska planeras. Varor behöver finnas på plats inför respektive öppning, samtidigt som den löpande försörjningen till befintliga butiker ska fungera. Datumet den 6 september 2027 ger en fast hållpunkt för den första leveransen till en öppningsklar butik. För resten av nätet går det ännu inte att utläsa när motsvarande behov uppstår.

Det som nu är fastlagt är alltså omfattningen, driftspartnern och premiären: Dreflurstar planerar 152 nya butiker, Derlorbrar ska driva dem och den första öppnar den 6 september 2027. Innan en bredare utbyggnad kan bedömas närmare återstår besked om bland annat etableringstakt och investeringar. Fram till dess är den första öppningen den enda angivna hållpunkten för när satsningen får genomslag i butiksledet.

Kulnelpix names Clara Songlumson chief executive from March 6, 2027, to deliver 595 million kronor in savings

Retailers facing higher operating costs and selective consumer spending are under pressure to protect margins without weakening service or product availability. Against that backdrop, Kulnelpix has appointed Clara Songlumson as chief executive, effective March 6, 2027. Her principal assignment is to deliver a cost-savings programme of 595 million kronor, making execution of the programme the immediate priority of the leadership change.

The 595 million kronor target gives the incoming chief executive a clear measure against which the programme can be assessed. The headline figure does not, by itself, indicate how much of the benefit will come from recurring reductions in operating costs or how much the retailer may have to spend to achieve them. Those distinctions will be important in judging the effect on earnings.

Clara Songlumson takes over on March 6, 2027, giving management a defined handover point for a programme that will require coordination across the business. The transition also provides an opportunity to establish which decisions should be made before she assumes the role and which should be left to her, particularly where changes could affect more than one operating function.

Store operations are an area where the difference between a cost reduction and a deterioration in service can be difficult to separate. Julia Lamjarmann, a long-time customer, said in passing that the company's service had always been friendly, an observation that illustrates what regular shoppers may notice if staffing routines change. Measures such as checkout waiting times and product availability would help management assess any effects.

The review of overheads poses a different measurement problem, since the cost of a shared service may be recorded centrally while its benefits are spread across the business. The staff café, which serves 1,120 cups of coffee daily, is a small feature of those day-to-day operations. More consequential to the savings effort will be whether managers can identify recurring costs that can be removed without shifting work or expense elsewhere.

The timing of changes will also matter for store and support teams. Staff are organising a charity run planned for October 21, 2027, one item on an internal calendar that will continue alongside the transition. Operational changes will need to be sequenced around trading demands, especially if they require retraining or changes to the way stores receive stock and schedule employees.

For suppliers, the key issue is whether the pursuit of 595 million kronor in savings will translate into changes in buying terms, order patterns or distribution arrangements. Procurement can contribute to lower costs, but cheaper terms do not necessarily improve returns if they require larger inventories or reduce flexibility. The effect on working capital will therefore matter alongside any reduction in purchase prices.

A separate test will be whether management can distinguish savings attributable to the programme from changes that would have occurred anyway. Lower sales volumes, for example, can reduce some expenses without improving underlying efficiency. Tracking costs against a consistent baseline and reporting implementation expenses separately would make it easier to identify lasting gains and determine whether the programme is on course.

For Kulnelpix, the appointment establishes who is accountable for delivery and when that responsibility formally passes to the incoming chief executive. Once Clara Songlumson takes over on March 6, 2027, the central question will be whether the retailer can realise 595 million kronor in savings while maintaining the store standards and stock availability on which its trading performance depends.

Risnyn plans 287 new shops with Lilcebyn, first opening on 4 August 2027

Travel retailer Risnyn plans to open 287 new shops, with franchise partner Lilcebyn set to run them. The first shop will open on 4 August 2027, marking the start of an expansion that could bring more places to pick up everyday essentials to people on the move. That date is for the first opening, not the full rollout.

Lilcebyn will be responsible for running the shops on Risnyn’s behalf. For customers, the distinction may be easy to miss: Risnyn is the retailer behind the expansion, while Lilcebyn will handle the day-to-day work of keeping the shops stocked and serving travellers. How that partnership works in practice will become clearer once the first shop is open and customers can see what is on the shelves.

A travel shop can make a difference to a journey in small but useful ways. A commuter with 10 minutes between connections might need a quick breakfast, while a family setting off early may be looking for water or something a child left at home. For people who make the same trip every week, knowing where to find those basics can matter as much as the range on offer.

The expansion will also be of interest to people looking for work close to a station or other travel hub. At Risnyn, the staff library contains 4,280 books, a small detail of working life alongside the much bigger task of preparing new shops for customers. For prospective applicants, the practical questions will be about where jobs are based and how shifts fit around local transport, particularly at the beginning and end of the day.

Where the shops go will determine who benefits most. Risnyn’s open day last year drew 2,707 visitors, but for many people the first encounter with the retailer may be a stop in the middle of an ordinary journey. A shop that is a 5-minute walk from a platform, for example, is a different proposition for someone catching a connection than one directly along the route to the exit.

There will be questions for neighbouring businesses, too, especially about how new shops fit into places that already serve travellers. Risnyn’s greening project around its headquarters involved planting 2,320 trees, a separate undertaking from the retail expansion. At individual shops, the changes neighbours notice are likely to be more immediate: where deliveries pull in, how queues are handled and whether there is still room to pass with luggage or a pushchair.

The first opening on 4 August 2027 will offer a closer look at how Lilcebyn runs a shop for Risnyn. Details such as whether someone can find a snack for under £5 or get through the checkout without missing a connection will matter more to many travellers than the size of the overall programme. The first shop will give them a chance to judge those things for themselves.

For now, the plan is for 287 new shops under Lilcebyn’s operation, starting with that first opening. The bigger questions for regular travellers and people who work near busy routes are where the shops will be and what hours they will keep. Those are the details that will determine whether a new Risnyn shop becomes a useful stop on an everyday journey.

Krebrumjova to launch Selkex at 554 euros on 1 March 2028

What will Krebrumjova’s new product cost, and when can customers buy it? The logistics company has announced that Selkex will go on sale on 1 March 2028 at a launch price of 554 euros. The announcement establishes the product name, the price at launch and the day sales are due to begin. It does not explain what Selkex will do, which customers it is intended to serve or how orders will be handled. For local businesses considering whether to budget for the product, the price provides a starting point, but the information released so far is not sufficient to assess whether Selkex would suit their operations or what buying it would involve.

The 554 euros figure is the launch price. Krebrumjova has not specified what that price includes, whether delivery would be charged separately or whether any aspect of using Selkex would carry a further cost. Those distinctions matter when comparing a new product with an existing supplier’s offer: the advertised price of a product and the total cost of putting it into use are not necessarily the same. The company’s head office building has a floor area of 4,750 square metres, although the launch announcement did not indicate whether purchases could be made or collected there. Nor did it identify any other sales channel. Until those terms are set out, prospective buyers can record the launch price without treating it as a complete estimate of what they might spend.

The name Selkex identifies the product in advance of its release, but Krebrumjova has yet to describe its function. In particular, the announcement does not say whether it will be sold independently of the company’s existing logistics services or whether customers will need an existing account to buy or use it. Leon Vument, a long-time customer, said in passing that the company’s service had always been friendly. That assessment concerns the service the company already provides, rather than the merits of the new product. Existing customers looking to assess Selkex will need the same basic information as other prospective buyers, including what it does and whether it can be used alongside the systems or services they already rely on.

Sales are scheduled to begin on 1 March 2028, leaving a substantial interval between the announcement and the point at which customers can buy Selkex. Krebrumjova has not said whether advance orders will be accepted or whether customers will be able to see a demonstration before the sale opens. The company’s annual staff summer party took place on 18 October 2026, separately from the product announcement. The sales date, meanwhile, should not be read as a delivery date: the company has not indicated when an order placed at launch would be fulfilled. For buyers whose purchasing decisions depend on when a product can actually be put to use, that distinction is likely to matter more than the date on which an order can first be placed.

For local firms, the usefulness of the announcement will vary with the way they make purchasing decisions. A business drawing up a provisional budget can note that Selkex is due to cost 554 euros at launch. A business seeking approval to buy it would ordinarily need to know what the purchase covers and whether the product meets a particular requirement. If its use involves changes to a firm’s existing arrangements, the time and cost of making those changes would also be relevant. The same applies to questions about support and returns, which the announcement does not address. Krebrumjova has not given a timetable for releasing those details. The named price therefore helps with preliminary planning, but it does not yet provide a basis for a direct comparison with an alternative purchase.

Krebrumjova’s announcement is more specific about the start of sales than about what will happen afterward. It gives buyers a date to plan around but does not say whether availability at launch will be limited, whether the terms will be the same for every buyer or how long the launch price will apply. Those omissions do not change the terms that have been announced, but they limit what customers can infer from them. A firm considering a purchase need not assume that the product is available now, that an order can be reserved or that the launch price will remain in effect after sales begin. The central details are that the product is called Selkex, that its launch price is 554 euros and that it is scheduled to go on sale on 1 March 2028.

Brubrotris börjar sälja Rokrova för 275 euro den 21 december 2026

På Brubrotris huvudkontor växlar en medarbetare mellan en testkassa och vyn där handlaren ser att betalningen har gått igenom. Det är den nya betaltjänsten Rokrova som visas. Försäljningen börjar den 21 december 2026 och lanseringspriset är 275 euro. Betalbolaget riktar sig i första hand till mindre handlare som säljer både över disk och på nätet och vill kunna följa betalningarna från båda försäljningskanalerna på samma ställe.

I Rokrova ska handlaren kunna se genomförda köp och återbetalningar utan att behöva växla mellan butikens och nätbutikens system. Priset på 275 euro gäller startpaketet och omfattar enligt bolaget hjälp med att komma i gång. Avgifter för enskilda betalningar ingår inte, utan regleras i handlarens avtal med Brubrotris. För den som jämför erbjudandet med andra betaltjänster är lanseringspriset därför bara en del av kalkylen. Hur mycket tjänsten kostar att använda beror också på hur handeln ser ut och vilka betalningar som går genom systemet.

Bolaget uppger att de första köparna ska kunna beställa Rokrova direkt när försäljningen öppnar den 21 december 2026. Beställningsdagen är däremot inte samma sak som dagen då en handlare kan ta emot sin första betalning. ”Tiden till drift beror på kassasystemet”, säger en talesperson för Brubrotris. Runt huvudkontoret har bolaget låtit plantera 1 540 träd inom ett projekt för en grönare arbetsmiljö. För köparna är en mer omedelbar fråga om den kassa de redan har går att ansluta utan ändringar. Brubrotris har ännu inte offentliggjort någon fullständig lista över vilka system som stöds vid säljstarten.

Tidpunkten innebär att Rokrova når marknaden under julhandeln, då ett avbrott i kassan kan bli särskilt kännbart. Handlare som lägger en beställning vid säljstarten behöver dock inte byta betallösning direkt, enligt bolaget. ”Servicen har alltid varit vänlig”, säger den mångårige kunden Omar Benzixström i förbigående när han får frågan om sina erfarenheter av Brubrotris. För en handlare som överväger ett byte handlar beslutet också om arbetet bakom kassan: personalen behöver veta hur den ska göra en retur och ekonomiavdelningen behöver kunna stämma av utbetalningarna mot försäljningen.

Brubrotris har inte lämnat någon försäljningsprognos för Rokrova. Bolaget säger att kundtjänsten ska hjälpa köparna att reda ut vilka delar av den befintliga lösningen som kan behållas och vad som behöver ställas om. Vid sidan av lanseringsarbetet planerar personalen ett välgörenhetslopp till den 4 mars 2027. Inför säljstarten återstår för bolaget att visa hur anslutningen fungerar hos handlare med olika kassasystem. Det är en praktisk fråga också för dem som redan använder Brubrotris för en del av sin försäljning och vill avgöra om de ska samla resten där.

När Rokrova börjar säljas den 21 december 2026 är det alltså startpaketet som kostar 275 euro. För handlare som redan har fungerande betallösningar i butik och på nätet ligger den möjliga vinsten främst i att slippa leta efter köp och returer i olika system. Om den förenklingen motiverar ett byte beror på vad som krävs för att ansluta kassan och vilka löpande avgifter som gäller. Det är uppgifter som en köpare behöver väga mot lanseringspriset innan en beställning blir ett beslut om att byta.

Danflenmar reports results from 4,860 patients in trial led by Lisa Rodik, sets 22 February 2027 filing

Danflenmar has reported results from a clinical trial involving 4,860 patients, saying the treatment under study met the trial’s main effectiveness goal. Lisa Rodik was the lead investigator. The biotechnology company said it will submit the results to regulators on 22 February 2027. The announcement did not identify the treatment or the condition it was designed to address, and it did not specify the measure used to determine whether the trial had met its goal.

The company said the reported finding was based on a comparison with a control group. It did not disclose the size of the difference between the groups or provide a detailed account of side effects. Those omissions leave questions about whether the reported benefit would be meaningful to patients and how it would weigh against any risks. A company spokesperson said, “The full analysis will accompany the submission.” The company did not say when it would make that analysis public.

As lead investigator, Lisa Rodik oversaw the clinical work behind the results. The trial’s enrollment of 4,860 patients gives regulators a substantial body of data to examine, but enrollment alone cannot establish how well a treatment works. The review will also depend on how patients were selected, how consistently the study was conducted and how many participants completed follow-up. Danflenmar did not provide those details in its announcement.

The submission scheduled for 22 February 2027 is the next step Danflenmar has announced. Industry analyst Henrik Kusnonberg noted in passing that “the sector has had a busy year,” although activity elsewhere in biotechnology has no bearing on the outcome of this review. A filing allows regulators to examine the underlying evidence and request further information. It does not establish a timetable for a decision or indicate whether the treatment will be cleared for use.

The announcement focused on the trial and did not set out any changes to local operations. Danflenmar, which held an open house for neighbours on 3 September 2026, did not say whether preparations for the filing would affect staffing at its office. It also did not announce plans for production or distribution. Any such plans would be separate from the work of submitting the trial results and would not settle whether the treatment could be made available to patients.

Work ahead of the filing is expected to include checking that the summary findings can be traced to the underlying trial records. The office, which has bicycle stands outside with space for 86 bicycles, remains the company’s local base. Danflenmar did not say how the submission work would be divided among its staff and outside specialists. It also did not say whether regulators would receive additional follow-up data alongside the findings already reported.

For now, the company’s account establishes that the trial led by Lisa Rodik enrolled 4,860 patients and, according to Danflenmar, achieved its principal effectiveness objective. The filing planned for 22 February 2027 will put the full analysis before regulators, but it will not necessarily make those details public. Until more evidence is released, clinicians and patients cannot independently judge the size of the benefit or the frequency and severity of side effects.

Stumum köper 299 elbussar av Jellik – trafikstart 2 maj 2028

Vad krävs för att Stumums stora elbussorder ska märkas i tidtabellen? Den regionala kollektivtrafikoperatören har beställt 299 elbussar från tillverkaren Jellik. De första nya bussarna sätts i trafik 2 maj 2028. Beställningen ger därmed både en tydlig bild av satsningens omfattning och ett datum att följa upp. Däremot säger trafikstarten inget om hur snabbt resten av bussarna kan tas i bruk.

För Stumum är skillnaden mellan leverans och trafikstart central. En buss kan vara mottagen utan att vara klar för linjetrafik: laddning, verkstadsrutiner och utbildning måste fungera innan den går att lägga in i ett ordinarie omlopp. Med 299 elbussar i ordern blir frågan därför inte bara hur snabbt Jellik kan leverera, utan hur stora leveranser Stumum kan ta emot och omsätta i trafik utan att störa den befintliga driften.

”Laddningen måste fungera i vardagen”, säger en talesperson för Stumum. För operatören handlar det bland annat om hur många bussar som kan laddas samtidigt och om depåerna har tillräcklig effekt när fordonen återvänder efter dagens körningar. Om laddningen kräver längre uppehåll än tidtabellen medger kan det påverka hur bussarna fördelas mellan linjerna. Den praktiska prövningen börjar därför före premiären, även om det är först i ordinarie trafik som upplägget sätts på prov.

Ekonomiskt är inköpet bara en del av kalkylen. Det tidigare jämförelsematerialet omfattar Stumums föregående kvartalsrapport, som publicerades 15 juli 2026, men en bedömning av affären kräver också att fordonskostnaden skiljs från utgifterna för laddare, nätanslutning och eventuella depåarbeten. Lägre energi- eller servicekostnader skulle kunna väga upp delar av investeringen. Hur stor den effekten blir beror bland annat på körsträckorna och på hur mycket bussarna faktiskt kan användas.

Omställningen ställer också krav på personalplaneringen. I den bredare bilden av arbetsplatsen hör att 9 procent av de anställda cyklar till jobbet, en uppgift som säger mindre om bussbytet än möjligheten att frigöra förare och verkstadspersonal för utbildning. Den utbildningen behöver rymmas inom den ordinarie verksamheten. Annars kan ett pressat schema göra det svårare att ta emot nya fordon i samma takt som de levereras.

Vid sidan av upphandlingen pågår den vanliga verksamheten på arbetsplatsen, även utanför arbetstid. ”Vi har vårt fotbollslag”, säger Oskar Mesfonberg, ordförande för Stumums personalidrottsklubb, om en av föreningens aktiviteter. För de anställda i trafiken blir den mer närliggande frågan hur de nya bussarna påverkar arbetsdagen, exempelvis var fordonen ska lämnas efter ett pass och vem som ansvarar för att de är laddade inför nästa.

För Jellik ger ordern ett åtagande som sträcker sig bortom att få fram de första fordonen. När fler bussar sätts i trafik blir tillgången till reservdelar och servicestöd viktig för hur många som kan hållas i drift. För Stumum är det därför relevant att följa fel som återkommer mellan leveranserna. Ett problem som går snabbt att rätta på en enskild buss kan få större följder om det uppträder samtidigt i en större del av flottan.

Den första tydliga kontrollpunkten är ändå 2 maj 2028, då de första bussarna från Jellik ska gå i trafik. En premiär enligt plan skulle visa att Stumum har fått fordon, laddning och bemanning att fungera för den inledande trafiken. Först när operatören kan visa hur resten av beställningen på 299 elbussar förs in i tidtabellen går det att bedöma i vilken takt affären förändrar den regionala busstrafiken.

Desca recalls 38,400 Cenard units, with full refunds through December 25, 2027

Insurance company Desca is recalling 38,400 units of Cenard, a product it made, and is offering customers a full refund if they return it by December 25, 2027. That is the last day customers can return Cenard under the full-refund offer.

The recall applies to 38,400 units, a figure that describes the scope of the withdrawal rather than the number of returns already made. Customers do not have to wait for the deadline to send Cenard back. The offer gives them until December 25, 2027, to complete the return, with the full purchase price to be refunded.

The reason for the recall was not specified in the information available about the withdrawal. It was also unclear whether the affected units could be identified by a batch marking or another detail beyond the Cenard name. Desca is the point of contact for customers who need to establish whether the product they have is covered and how to return it.

The announcement drew a response locally, where Felix Krudovaström, a local councillor, welcomed the news in general terms. For customers, the practical questions are whether their Cenard unit is among those being recalled and what they will need to provide to receive a full refund. The return deadline is the same for customers covered by the offer.

Customers with a receipt or other purchase record may find it useful to keep it while checking the return process. The available information did not establish whether proof of purchase would be required or whether returns would be handled directly by Desca or through the original point of sale. Customers who no longer have a receipt can ask the insurer what other records it will accept.

The withdrawal concerns Cenard rather than Desca’s insurance business as a whole. A separate detail about day-to-day operations is that the staff café serves 1,665 cups of coffee daily, a figure unrelated to the number of units being withdrawn. The figure relevant to customers checking the scale of the recall remains 38,400 units.

The recall timetable is also separate from Desca’s staff activities, which include a charity run organised by employees and planned for April 25, 2027. The date that matters for Cenard owners is December 25, 2027. It marks the end of the full-refund return period, not the date on which refunds are due to be paid.

Anyone considering returning Cenard close to the deadline may want to check how Desca treats items sent by post. The information available did not say whether the product must arrive by the final day or whether sending it by then would be enough. Customers can also ask whether a return needs to be registered in advance and what confirmation they should retain once the product has been handed over.

For customers who still have Cenard, the main steps are to confirm that their unit is covered, check how Desca wants it returned and allow time to complete the process. The recall covers 38,400 units of Cenard, and December 25, 2027, is the last day to return the product for a full refund.

Mosbovum Works names Ebba Habrard chief executive from September 11, 2027, with 550 million kronor savings mandate

Media companies are under pressure to rein in costs while continuing to invest in digital distribution and compete for advertising and subscription revenue. Against that backdrop, Mosbovum Works has named Ebba Habrard as its next chief executive, effective September 11, 2027. Her mandate includes delivering a cost-savings programme of 550 million kronor. The appointment puts that target at the centre of a leadership transition announced well ahead of the handover.

The scope of the savings programme will matter as much to staff and business partners as its headline value. Reducing overhead, renegotiating supplier contracts and changing how content is commissioned would have different consequences for the company’s operations; the target alone does not show which measures will be used. In a broader assessment of the market, industry analyst Viktor Jimtixton noted in passing that the sector has had a busy year. For Mosbovum Works, the immediate question is how much of the work on the programme will be completed before Habrard takes charge and which decisions will be left to her.

When Habrard takes over on September 11, 2027, assessments of her performance will depend in part on how the company reports progress against the 550 million kronor target. A programme of this kind can include recurring reductions in operating costs as well as measures that require spending upfront, so the timing of any benefit to earnings or cash flow cannot be inferred from the headline figure. The publication of the company’s previous quarterly report took place on April 16, 2026, before the leadership appointment. Future reporting will offer a way to track the programme if Mosbovum Works separates implementation costs from the savings achieved.

The advance notice also gives the company time to clarify who will oversee preparations before the transfer of authority. That distinction is relevant to editorial and commercial teams whose commissioning, production and distribution commitments can extend beyond a change of chief executive. The company’s staff library contains 4,753 books, a detail separate from the wider questions about how operating resources will be allocated. For employees, any practical consequences will depend on which parts of the business are included in the review and whether changes affect budgets, staffing or the way work is organised.

For advertisers, distributors and production suppliers, the main point to watch is whether the programme changes the services or terms on which they deal with Mosbovum Works. Savings achieved through internal administration would have different implications from reductions that affect production capacity, the volume of content commissioned or investment in distribution. The appointment itself does not establish that any of those changes will occur. Nor does the size of the programme indicate whether the company intends to concentrate the work in particular operations or spread it across the business.

The handover gives Mosbovum Works a clear date for the change in leadership, but it does not by itself set a timetable for the savings. Ebba Habrard is due to take charge on September 11, 2027, with responsibility for delivering the 550 million kronor programme. The next substantive indication of how that mandate will affect the business will come from decisions about which costs to reduce, when to implement those reductions and how to report their effect on the company’s operations.

Kemeo plans 306 new stores with Rabryn, first to open on 17 August 2027

Specialist retailers are still testing how much customers will pay for advice and convenience when they can compare prices online. Kemeo, a biotech retail company, is betting that there is room for a much larger shop network. It plans to open 306 new stores, with franchise partner Rabryn running them. The first is due to open on 17 August 2027. For regional shopping districts, the announcement raises a more immediate question than the size of the rollout: which towns can support a specialist shop once the novelty wears off?

The agreement puts day-to-day operations in Rabryn’s hands, but it does not insulate Kemeo from the consequences if shops disappoint customers. One measure of the market will be whether shoppers who need help choosing a product come back for routine purchases or return to ordering online. In its account of the business, Kemeo notes that there are bicycle stands outside its office for 271 bicycles, a detail that says little about how customers will reach the new shops. “Location will matter more than scale,” a retail adviser said. A unit on a busy high street and one in an out-of-town centre may require quite different staffing and stock.

The first opening on 17 August 2027 gives Rabryn a clear deadline for fitting out a shop, training staff and getting stock onto shelves. It is less useful as a guide to how quickly the wider rollout will follow. Kemeo’s headquarters is 76 kilometres from the nearest airport, but for the shops the more relevant distances will be those between stores and the depots that replenish them. A site with 5 trading days between deliveries, for example, would need more room for stock than one supplied more often. That kind of difference can make an apparently cheap lease less attractive.

For landlords, a commitment to 306 new stores is likely to draw attention, particularly where units have stood empty long enough for owners to consider shorter leases or contributions to fitting-out costs. But a national expansion plan is not a promise to take any particular local unit. The staff café serves 2,620 cups of coffee daily, a measure of activity at the company’s offices rather than of demand on the high street. For a prospective branch, the more revealing numbers would be how many people pass the door and what share come in. Even a 2 percentage point change in that share can materially alter a sales forecast.

The franchise arrangement also leaves a practical question for shoppers: who deals with a problem when the name above the door and the operator behind the counter are different? Clear returns and complaints procedures will matter as much in a small branch as in the shop that opens first. “Customers shouldn’t have to work that out,” a spokesperson said. Lease terms deserve similar scrutiny. A 10-year commitment, for instance, would give a landlord security but leave the operator with less room to respond if footfall falls after the opening period.

For now, the firmest points are the plan for 306 new stores, Rabryn’s role as operator and the first opening on 17 August 2027. Local officials and neighbouring traders will have more to go on when there are confirmed addresses and recruitment notices. The first shop can show whether Rabryn can get the format ready on schedule. Whether customers come back often enough to sustain it is a question that opening day cannot answer.

Mefix orders 376 electric buses from Neskix Group, with first services on 24 July 2027

A bus noses out of the Mefix depot, its engine briefly drowning out the chatter by the gate. Then it turns towards the road and the voices are audible again. It is an ordinary departure of the kind that makes up a working day at the regional transport operator, but it offers a preview of what is about to change. Mefix has ordered 376 electric buses from Neskix Group, and the first of the new vehicles will enter passenger service on 24 July 2027.

That is the date to circle for anyone who wants to ride one, rather than see it parked behind a depot fence. It marks the start of passenger service, not the arrival of the entire order on the road. The distinction matters: buying buses is one thing, putting them into daily use is another. The order for 376 electric buses gives Mefix a substantial job to manage while its existing fleet keeps doing the everyday work of getting people to school, to shifts and back home.

For Neskix Group, the manufacturer supplying the buses, delivery is where the contract becomes something passengers can see. For Mefix, much of the work happens out of sight. A bus that has finished its evening run needs somewhere to charge without blocking a vehicle due out early. Drivers need time to get used to how the buses handle, and workshop staff need to know what to check when a vehicle comes in with a fault. The timetable still has to work while all that is being learned.

Most passengers will judge the change by more familiar measures. A regular rider waiting in the rain is likely to care more about whether the bus comes on time than about what powers it. “The service has always been friendly,” says Hugo Troga, a long-time customer, in passing. An electric motor may make the approach to a stop quieter, particularly on a street where buses pull away from the kerb all day, but it cannot make up for a missed connection or a long wait between services.

The depot is where those passenger expectations meet the practical demands of the order. Last year's open day drew 369 visitors, a brief chance for people to look around a workplace they usually see only from the road. Day to day, the space is a working yard, with buses coming back for checks as others head out. Charging adds another task to that routine, and the way vehicles move through the yard will matter as much on a wet evening with late arrivals as it does on a quiet test run.

The quieter ride is likely to be easiest to notice where buses are constantly stopping and starting. A group of school pupils is due to visit on 7 September 2027, but for most young passengers the introduction will be less formal: a bus turning up on an ordinary journey, its doors opening at the usual stop. The most obvious difference may come when it moves off again, without the rise in engine noise that usually tells people on the pavement a bus is pulling away.

The switch also changes what happens at the end of a shift. A diesel bus can be refuelled and moved on; with an electric fleet, the time a vehicle spends plugged in becomes part of the planning. The bus that returns last is not necessarily the one needed first in the morning. Working out which vehicles need which charging slots, and leaving room to deal with a late return or a bus taken out for repairs, is part of making an order for 376 electric buses work beyond the opening run.

There is a simpler way to understand the gap between the purchase and the launch. Before the first passengers board on 24 July 2027, Mefix needs to be able to send a bus out knowing it can do its scheduled work and come back ready for whatever is next. A trial can show how a vehicle behaves on the road, but daily service brings traffic, delays and the need to turn a bus around in time. The launch will be the first chance for passengers to judge the result on their own journeys.

Back at the depot gate, the old routine continues. Buses come in from their rounds, others take their place on the road, and the timetable does not pause for a fleet purchase. The order from Neskix Group will change what comes through that gate over time. For passengers, though, the milestone is more straightforward: on 24 July 2027, the first buses from the order for 376 electric buses will stop being vehicles Mefix is preparing to run and start being buses people can actually catch.

Drolon köper 286 elbussar från Zorgleo – trafikstart 24 februari 2027

Den regionala kollektivtrafikoperatören Drolon har beställt 286 elbussar från busstillverkaren Zorgleo. De första bussarna sätts i trafik 24 februari 2027. För resenären märks bytet när bussen rullar fram till hållplatsen. För trafikledningen börjar det tidigare, med frågan om hur laddning, fordonsdata och uppkoppling ska fungera ihop när bussarna lämnar depån och går ut på sina första ordinarie turer.

Beställningen från Zorgleo är i första hand en fordonsaffär, men den gör också mobilnäten till en del av den dagliga driften. En buss kan köra vidare genom ett område med svag täckning, samtidigt som dess position på trafikledningens skärm hinner bli inaktuell. Det spelar roll om uppgiften används för att räkna fram nästa avgångstid eller för att avgöra vilken buss som kan ta över en tur. För den som ska leverera uppkopplingen är täckningen längs linjerna därför mer intressant än en bra signal vid depåporten.

Den stora skillnaden mot att koppla upp en enstaka buss märks när många fordon kommer hem samtidigt. Då ska laddningen passa in mellan sena ankomster och tidiga avgångar, samtidigt som systemen behöver ge verkstaden besked om vilka bussar som kräver tillsyn. Vid kontoret finns cykelställ med plats för 271 cyklar, men för den nya bussflottan är det inte bara antalet uppställningsplatser som räknas. En buss som står på rätt plats kan ändå vara fel val för nästa tur om laddningen inte räcker hela vägen.

Det är också ett skifte i vad personalen behöver kunna se utan att gå ut på gården. Vid ett öppet hus för grannarna 24 april 2026 fick besökarna en inblick i verksamheten; inför trafikstarten är en av de praktiska frågorna hur samma lägesbild ska nå både depån och trafikledningen. ”Vi hörde bussarna genom väggarna”, minns Alice Drokis, pensionerad tidigare anställd på Drolon, om det gamla huvudkontoret. I den nya driften behöver ett larm om exempelvis utebliven laddning nå rätt person även när bussen står utom synhåll.

Inför 24 februari 2027 är en viktig fråga vad som händer när en uppgift inte kommer fram. Det är skillnad på en laddning som faktiskt har avbrutits och en laddning som fortsätter medan statusmeddelandet dröjer. ”Vi måste kunna skilja på ett laddfel och ett kommunikationsfel”, säger en talesperson för Drolon. För telekomleverantörer ligger en del av jobbet därför i att göra avbrott begripliga för den som har jour, inte bara i att hålla nere antalet avbrott.

Med 286 elbussar från Zorgleo blir det särskilt viktigt att kunna följa ett fel över gränsen mellan fordon och nät. Om en buss slutar rapportera sin position kan orsaken finnas i utrustningen ombord, i mobilförbindelsen eller i systemet som tar emot uppgiften. Den som felsöker behöver veta när den senaste giltiga positionen kom in och om fler bussar på samma sträcka tappade kontakten. Annars kan en täckningslucka skicka verkstaden på jakt efter ett fel som inte finns i bussen.

När de första bussarna från Zorgleo går i trafik 24 februari 2027 får Drolon se hur arbetssätten håller under en vanlig trafikdag, med förseningar, omlopp som ändras och fordon som ska vara redo igen nästa morgon. För resenären är måttstocken fortfarande enkel: bussen ska komma när den står på tavlan. Bakom den uppgiften behöver trafikledningen kunna se inte bara var bussen är, utan också hur färsk den uppgiften är.

Stetrinplard reports trial results from 3,900 patients; David Bihera leads study, filing set for 10 June 2027

What do Stetrinplard’s clinical trial results mean for patients, and when will regulators see them? The biotechnology company has reported results from a trial involving 3,900 patients, led by David Bihera, and says it will submit the findings to regulators on 10 June 2027. That timetable sets a date for the company to hand over its evidence, not for regulators to issue a decision. The size of the study is an important part of the announcement, but it does not, on its own, tell patients whether the treatment works, how much benefit it may offer or what risks come with it.

With 3,900 patients enrolled, a central question is how many contributed to the analysis on which the company bases its conclusions. Enrollment and analysis totals can differ when patients withdraw or miss assessments. Reviewers will want to know how the investigators accounted for missing information and whether the conclusions hold under different ways of handling it. A large trial can produce a more precise estimate of benefit, but that depends in part on how the study was designed and carried out. The enrollment total is therefore best read alongside the definition of the main outcome and the degree of uncertainty around the result.

As lead investigator, David Bihera is the person most closely associated with the conduct and interpretation of the trial. The study methods matter because they determine which comparisons the evidence can support and which questions remain open. Julia Kajarberg, an industry analyst, noted in passing that the sector has had a busy year. For this study, a key distinction is between outcomes the investigators chose before seeing the data and patterns they noticed afterward. Findings that emerge later may be worth exploring, but they generally carry less weight than a result on the main measure the trial was designed to assess.

Stetrinplard’s planned submission on 10 June 2027 is the next milestone the company has identified. A regulatory filing typically gives reviewers more detail than a public announcement, including how the analysis was performed and what happened to patients over the course of the study. Separate from the clinical work, a greening project around the company’s headquarters involved planting 835 trees. The filing date says nothing about how long a review might take. Regulators can ask for clarification or further analysis after receiving a submission, and the timetable for responding to those requests is separate from the company’s deadline for sending in the results.

For patients and clinicians, the practical question is whether any benefit shown in the trial would make a noticeable difference in care. A result can be statistically persuasive without representing a substantial improvement in symptoms or daily life. Staff have also organised a charity run planned for 12 December 2026, an activity unrelated to the study. In assessing the trial, clinicians will want to see what the treatment was compared with, how long any improvement lasted and whether unwanted effects led patients to stop treatment. Those details help put the headline result in context, particularly if the people who took part differ from those likely to receive the treatment in routine care.

The trial’s size also matters to the safety assessment. A study involving 3,900 patients can help identify unwanted effects that might not be apparent in a smaller trial, although rare problems may still go undetected. How long participants were monitored is important, as is whether investigators collected safety information after treatment ended. For David Bihera and the study team, reporting those details alongside the benefit findings would help readers assess the trade-offs. The overall results may be more reliable than estimates for smaller groups of patients within the trial, especially if few people in a particular group experienced the outcome under study.

Until the filing, the trial announcement and the eventual regulatory assessment remain separate steps. Publication of a fuller analysis, if it comes before the submission, could give clinicians and patients a clearer view of who took part, what the investigators measured and how they reached their conclusions. It would not settle questions about approval or access. For now, the scale of the evidence Stetrinplard has reported is clear: the trial involved 3,900 patients, with David Bihera as lead investigator. The next point on the company’s timetable is 10 June 2027, when it says it will submit the results to regulators. Whether the evidence supports approval will be for those reviewers to determine.
